findings.summary: A failed final flush of the 64 KiB write buffer escaped WriteAsync from DisposeAsync and replaced the WriteFailed/Stopped outcome with NotConnected and a null path, so the NoSpace (exit 13) mapping never reached the caller
findings.evidence: expected: a failed final flush keeps the outcome WriteFailed with the path and the NoSpace note | actual: WriteAsync now closes the file in TryCloseAsync (once on every path), a dispose IOException is noted and logged and the outcome is WriteFailed unless the body already returned it; read by re-audit reader RA-A; scripts/check.ps1 PASS (27 checks, 1 skipped; tests run=4440 skipped=0) in a pristine clone of 43d7af9

findings.summary: CompleteExit blocked the UI thread on ActivationPipeListener.DisposeAsync().GetResult() with no deadline while the listener awaits command handlers whose continuations need that thread, so closing the window during a waiting play, resume or record command hung the exit (also reported as S6-1 by a second auditor)
findings.evidence: expected: the exit never waits on the command listener without the dispatcher pumping and without a bound | actual: CompleteExit waits with WaitPumping(listener.DisposeAsync, max(RemainingCloseTime, 500 ms)) and logs SHUTDOWN DEADLINE path=listener on timeout; read by re-audit reader RA-B, source test ReleaseAuditSp0246SourceTests.S6_1 updated; scripts/check.ps1 PASS (27 checks, 1 skipped; tests run=4440 skipped=0) in a pristine clone of 43d7af9

findings.summary: The person's Stop all went through StopAllCoreAsync, which never unchose the stopped sources, so with start-with-application on they restarted at the next launch although StopAsync unchooses one source
findings.evidence: expected: Stop all unchooses every source it stops and no other cause does | actual: StopAllCoreAsync calls SaveChosenAsync(source, chosen:false) after each teardown only when cause == Person; ApplicationExit, SignOut, SettingsChanged and the LAN port change keep the choice (callers traced by re-audit reader RA-A); scripts/check.ps1 PASS (27 checks, 1 skipped; tests run=4440 skipped=0) in a pristine clone of 43d7af9

findings.summary: ApplyAcceptsRestrictedCommandsFromSettingsAsync ignored a failed state write, so turning the restricted-commands switch off during a failed write left the guard on while the checkbox showed off
findings.evidence: expected: the guard fails closed whenever the person has turned the switch off | actual: MainWindow.AcceptsRestrictedCommands is the committed value unless a revocation is pending, set before the write and cleared only after a save that agrees; the three readers use it; scripts/check.ps1 PASS (27 checks, 1 skipped; tests run=4440 skipped=0) in a pristine clone of 43d7af9

findings.summary: Re-audit of the S4-1 fix: a stale earlier on-toggle write that landed while a later off-toggle was still pending cleared the revocation the off-toggle had set, so the guard could stay open after two quick toggles
findings.evidence: expected: only the newest toggle may clear the revocation | actual: a request counter (_restrictedCommandsRequest) is compared before the flag is cleared; the two-toggle trace (on then off, off write failing) keeps the guard closed; reviewed by the lead after RA-B; scripts/check.ps1 PASS (27 checks, 1 skipped; tests run=4440 skipped=0) in a pristine clone of 43d7af9

play and volume set run without the load/busy guard that channel add uses, so a command in the first second of start-up gets a wrong final answer instead of busy
